symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Number of observed system variables.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: Indices of the observed variables.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of nonobservational regimes.

symbols.name: Kcal
symbols.def: Regime indices, with zero denoting observation.

symbols.name: Kplus
symbols.def: Indices of the explicitly nonobservational soft-intervention regimes.

symbols.name: zeta
symbols.def: Exogenous indicator vertex for nonobservational regime \(k\); no intervention-indicator vertex exists at index zero.

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: Generic member of Dai et al.'s causally sufficient model family.

symbols.name: Seta
symbols.def: Binary selection nodes in candidate model \(\eta\).

symbols.name: Geta
symbols.def: Candidate causal DAG before intervention and selection conditioning.

symbols.name: Ieta
symbols.def: Candidate target family with the observational target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\) separated from the unknown nonobservational targets.

symbols.name: Tw
symbols.def: Dai et al.'s selected observational graph at index zero and basal-world interventional twin DAGs only at nonzero indices.

symbols.name: Mproj
symbols.sig: \(\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0))=\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}\) on \(V\), and \(\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k))=\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\) on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\)
symbols.def: Regime-specific MAG projection, with a distinct indicator-free observational branch and indicator-retaining nonobservational branches.

symbols.name: Meq
symbols.def: Two MAGs are related when they have the same adjacencies, unshielded colliders, and collider status on every common discriminating path.

symbols.name: Mfam
symbols.def: Supplied population-oracle MAG representatives: \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) is on \(V\), and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\).

symbols.name: Ccal
symbols.def: All candidate models satisfying the published causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection semantics and whose regime twin MAGs are Markov equivalent to the supplied representatives.

symbols.name: Ecal
symbols.def: Ordered incidence positions \(e=(k,u;uv)\) over the common regime skeletons, one position for each endpoint of each adjacency.

symbols.name: mark
symbols.def: Tail or arrowhead at endpoint position \(e\) in a fully oriented MAG.

symbols.name: PSI
symbols.def: Canonical SI-PAG family whose endpoint marks are the marks invariant over \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), with a circle at every noninvariant endpoint.

symbols.name: Pinit
symbols.def: The matrix-encoded family obtained by orienting unshielded colliders in every regime and intervention-indicator tails only in regimes indexed by \(\mathcal K_+\); all further within- and cross-regime orientations are delegated to \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\).

symbols.name: Hext
symbols.def: Technique handle combining discriminating-path closure, twin-graph descendant and ancestral-selection labels, and realizability-preserving paired completions.

symbols.name: RSI
symbols.def: Finite rule system to be derived by \(\texttt{oeq:si-extension-calculus}\), containing ordinary within-regime FCI rules and twin-compatible cross-regime rules from handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{ext}}\).

symbols.name: Cl
symbols.def: Least fixed point obtained by repeatedly replacing a circle endpoint by a tail or arrowhead using a rule in \(\mathsf R\), never deleting an adjacency or reversing a fixed mark.

symbols.name: Nend
symbols.def: Maximum number of endpoint positions over one observational graph on \(D\) vertices and \(K\) intervention graphs on \(D+1\) vertices.

symbols.name: Lin
symbols.def: Number of entries in one \(D\)-vertex observational adjacency-mark matrix and \(K\) nonobservational \(D+1\)-vertex adjacency-mark matrices.

symbols.name: arule
symbols.def: Number of regime placeholders in the finite code of rule \(r\).

symbols.name: brule
symbols.def: Number of vertex placeholders in the finite code of rule \(r\).

symbols.name: Trule
symbols.def: Worst-case time for one exhaustive match scan of finitely coded rule \(r\), including cubic-time graph searches for its path premises.

symbols.name: Tclose
symbols.def: Total time to materialize the initial family and run successful rule scans plus the final no-update scan on the encoded oracle MAG family.

symbols.name: Rcert
symbols.def: Finite certificate consisting of a DAG on \(V\), a set of distinct selection-parent sets, and one unknown target set for each nonobservational regime.

symbols.name: CheckDai
symbols.def: Accepts exactly when the certificate-generated regime MAG family matches the supplied adjacency and unshielded-collider patterns.

symbols.name: CDIScmp
symbols.def: Enumerates normalized Dai certificates, accepts them with \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}\), and returns endpointwise feasible-mark invariance together with opposing certificates for every circle; it returns an incompatibility flag if no certificate passes.

assumptions.condition: For candidate \(\eta\), \(\mathcal G_\eta\) is a finite directed acyclic graph on \(V\cup S_\eta\).
Candidate \(\eta\) contains no latent common cause of two vertices in \(V\).

standard.name: Dai et al. binary selection-node convention

assumptions.condition: Every vertex in \(S_\eta\) has no child in \(\mathcal G_\eta\).

standard.name: Dai et al. childless selection nodes

assumptions.condition: Every parent in \(\mathcal G_\eta\) of a vertex in \(S_\eta\) belongs to \(V\).

standard.name: Dai et al. observed-parent selection nodes

assumptions.condition: The observed stratum for candidate \(\eta\) conditions on \(S_\eta=\mathbf 1\).
The conditioned selection-node set in \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) and in \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) equals the basal copy \(S_\eta^*\).
The observational regime has empty intervention target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\).
For each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), every structural mechanism outside \(I_\eta^{(k)}\) and its exogenous input are shared with the basal world.
The indicator-free observational projection \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}\) on \(V\) is Markov equivalent to the supplied observational representative \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\).
For every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the projected twin MAG \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\) on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) is Markov equivalent to the supplied nonobservational representative \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\).
The supplied family has at least one compatible model: \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Separated observational and interventional twin graphs
definitions.construction: Define \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) as the indicator-free selected observational DAG on reality vertices \(X_V\) and basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\): copy \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) onto \(X_V\), copy each selection-parent edge into \(S_\eta^*\), and introduce no basal system copy, shared-noise vertex, or intervention-indicator vertex. Separately, for each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), form \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) on reality vertices \(X_V\), basal copies \(X_i^*\) and shared noises \(\varepsilon_i\) for \(i\in\operatorname{de}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(I_\eta^{(k)})\), basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\), and \(\zeta_k\). Copy each edge of \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) into each available world, route unaffected parents into affected basal children, copy selection-parent edges only into \(S_\eta^*\), add \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i^*\), and add \(\zeta_k\to X_i\) exactly for \(i\in I_\eta^{(k)}\).

definitions.name: Regime MAG projection
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0);X_V,\varnothing,S_\eta^*)\), retaining exactly \(V\) and no intervention indicator. Separately, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k);X_V\cup\{\zeta_k\},X^*\cup\varepsilon,S_\eta^*)\). In either branch, join two retained vertices exactly when an inducing path exists after the stated marginalization and conditioning, then place a tail at an endpoint exactly when that endpoint is an ancestor of the other endpoint or of \(S_\eta^*\), and an arrowhead otherwise.

definitions.name: Regime endpoint domain
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E(\mathbf M)=\{(k,u;uv):k\in\mathcal K,\ uv\in E(\mathcal M^{(k)}),\ u\in\{u,v\}\}\).

definitions.name: Canonical SI-PAG
definitions.construction: For each \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), set \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=a\in\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}\) when \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)})=a\) for every \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), and set \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\circ\) otherwise; retain the common regime skeletons.

definitions.name: Initial regime family
definitions.construction: On the observational skeleton on \(V\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders. On each nonobservational skeleton indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders and every endpoint at the existing indicator \(\zeta_k\) as a tail. No indicator endpoint is introduced in regime zero. Store the resulting family as adjacency and endpoint-mark matrices \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\); ordinary FCI closure and cross-regime propagation are both performed by \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\).

definitions.name: Twin-compatible extension handle
definitions.construction: Handle: start from the ordinary discriminating-path and uncovered-path closure inside each regime; attach the descendant and ancestral-selection labels forced by Dai et al.'s twin-MAG lemmas; propagate only label consequences shared across regimes; then adapt Jaber et al.'s I-MAG realizability lemma and Zhang's circle-component completion to construct, for a chosen unresolved endpoint, one tail completion and one arrowhead completion that are projections of a single common basal DAG with one ordered unknown-target family.

definitions.name: Finite oracle-MAG encoding
definitions.construction: Encode \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) by one \(D\times D\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\), and encode each \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\), \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), by one \((D+1)\times(D+1)\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The representation length is \(L_{\mathrm{in}}=D^2+K(D+1)^2\), and regime zero has no row or column for an indicator.

definitions.name: Finite SI-rule encoding and matcher
definitions.construction: Encode each \(r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) by a finite tuple of \(a_r\) typed regime placeholders, \(b_r\) typed vertex placeholders, adjacency and endpoint-mark premises, finite-state uncovered-path or discriminating-path predicates, and a nonempty list of circle-to-tail or circle-to-arrow updates. Regime placeholders are typed as either \(\{0\}\) or \(\mathcal K_+\), and an indicator term may occur only with the latter type. Match \(r\) by enumerating its regime and vertex assignments and deciding every path predicate by breadth-first search on its finite product-state graph. One exhaustive scan has cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\).

definitions.name: Monotone rule closure
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R}(\mathcal P)=\bigvee_{t\ge0}\mathsf R^t(\mathcal P)\), where the join is taken in the endpoint information order \(\circ\prec\mathrm{tail}\) and \(\circ\prec\mathrm{arrow}\), and every strict step fixes at least one previously circular endpoint.

definitions.name: Oracle-input closure schedule
definitions.construction: Materialize \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\) from the encoded oracle family by enumerating triples, then scan the finitely encoded rules in a fixed order and apply every consistent match found in a scan. Repeat after each scan that makes at least one strict endpoint update and stop after the first no-update scan. Record the certificate consisting of the ordered strict updates and the terminal no-match result. Its runtime envelope is \(T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)=O((K+1)(D+1)^3+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K))\).

definitions.name: Complete population CDIS
definitions.construction:
Enumerate in a fixed lexicographic order all normalized Dai certificates \(\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\) and retain precisely those satisfying \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\).  If none passes, return the flag \(\mathsf{incompatible}\).  Otherwise, for every \(e=(k,u;uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), form the nonempty feasible-mark set
\[
B_e(\mathbf M)=\left\{\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\bigr):\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\right\}\subseteq\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]
Set the output mark at \(e\) to the unique element when \(B_e(\mathbf M)\) is a singleton and to a circle when it contains both marks.  For every circle, retain the first accepted tail certificate and the first accepted arrowhead certificate in the enumeration order.  Define \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)\) to be this partial-graph family together with those coupled certificates.  Its observational component is on \(V\); only a component indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).

definitions.name: Normalized Dai certificate
definitions.construction:
A normalized Dai certificate is a tuple
\[
\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}),
\]
where \(E\) is a directed acyclic graph on \(V\), \(H\subseteq 2^V\) is a set of distinct subsets of \(V\), and \(T_k\subseteq V\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\); set \(T_0=\varnothing\).  A member \(h\in H\) represents the parent set of one binary childless selection node, and \(T_k\) represents the unknown soft-intervention target in regime \(k\).  In particular, \(|H|\le 2^D\).

definitions.name: Finite Dai-certificate checker
definitions.construction:
For a normalized certificate \(\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\), set
\[
A(\mathcal R)=\operatorname{an}_E\!\left(\bigcup_{h\in H}h\right),
\qquad
F_k(\mathcal R)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k).
\]
Construct a fully oriented family \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R)=(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R),\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)}(\mathcal R))\) as follows.  The observational graph \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) has vertex set \(V\).  Distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when at least one of the following holds:
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E;
\quad
\exists c\in A(\mathcal R):\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E;
\quad
\exists h\in H:\ \{i,j\}\subseteq h.
\]
At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A(\mathcal R)\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A(\mathcal R)\) and every internal vertex \(v_1,\ldots,v_{m-1}\) belongs to \(F_k(\mathcal R)\).  Also, \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k\cup\bigl(F_k(\mathcal R)\cap A(\mathcal R)\bigr),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the following exhaustive cases:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k(\mathcal R)&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ i\notin F_k(\mathcal R)\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ j\notin F_k(\mathcal R)\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k(\mathcal R),\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same set of unshielded collider triples; otherwise set the checker to zero.  All ancestry, descendant, connectivity, adjacency, and unshielded-collider tests are finite matrix computations.  Regime zero introduces no indicator, whereas only \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) uses \(\zeta_k\).

statements.statement: For any finite \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) represented by \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\) and monotone in the endpoint information order, the schedule in \(\texttt{def:closure-runtime-certificate}\) terminates after at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}=D(D-1)+KD(D+1)\) strict endpoint updates and one terminal no-update scan. Rule \(r\) is matched in \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\) time, and the total oracle-input orientation runtime is \(T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)=O((K+1)(D+1)^3+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K))\), which is polynomial in the finite input dimensions because the rule set and every \(a_r,b_r\) are fixed independently of \(D,K\).
statements.justification: The per-rule matcher and endpoint potential turn finite closure into a checkable total runtime certificate on the supplied oracle graphs.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention gives iterative CDIS pseudocode but no finite rule encoding, per-rule matching cost, or oracle-input closure runtime.
statements.consumer: A population implementation can audit every orientation scan and certify polynomial mark propagation without a complexity claim for discovering the oracle MAGs.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The observational matrix has at most \(D(D-1)\) ordered endpoint positions, and the \(K\) nonobservational matrices have at most \(KD(D+1)\) such positions.  Hence the total number of positions at which a circle can be replaced is at most
\[
N_{\mathrm{end}}=D(D-1)+KD(D+1).
\]
By the monotonicity hypothesis and \(\texttt{def:monotone-closure}\), a strict update replaces at least one circle by a tail or an arrowhead, and no later update can erase or reverse that mark.  Thus the endpoint potential, defined as the number of circular positions, decreases by at least one at every strict update and is initially at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\).  There are consequently at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) strict endpoint updates, at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) scans that make an update, and exactly one final scan that certifies that no rule matches consistently.

For a fixed rule \(r\), \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\) enumerates at most \((K+1)^{a_r}\) assignments of its typed regime placeholders and at most \((D+1)^{b_r}\) assignments of its vertex placeholders.  Its finite-state path predicates are decided on product-state graphs of size polynomial in \(D+1\); the stipulated cubic envelope gives
\[
T_r(D,K)=O\!\left((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3}\right).
\]
Materializing the initial family by enumerating triples costs \(O((K+1)(D+1)^3)\).  Summing one exhaustive match scan for every rule over at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) successful scans and the terminal unsuccessful scan yields
\[
T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)
=O\!\left((K+1)(D+1)^3
+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K)\right).
\]
The rule list and the integers \(a_r,b_r\) are fixed independently of \(D,K\), so the displayed expression is polynomial in \(D,K\), hence also in the finite matrix-input dimensions.  This argument is conditional on the separately supplied finite monotone rule list; it asserts no semantic completeness property and uses no conditional-independence discovery bound. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{ext}}\), can one construct a finite within- and cross-regime rule system \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D,K\), such that every rule has the typed finite representation in \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\), has per-scan cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\), and is sound over \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\); and such that for every endpoint \(e\) left circular by \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M))\) there exist \(\eta_e^{\mathrm t},\eta_e^{\mathrm a}\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) whose indicator-free observational projection and indicator-bearing nonobservational projections agree with every fixed closure mark while realizing respectively a tail and an arrowhead at \(e\)?
statements.justification: The paired global extension is the first proof step not supplied by ordinary FCI, unknown-intervention FCI, or Dai's soundness argument.
statements.gap: Zhang2008CompleteFCI constructs witnesses for one MAG class and JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020 realizes one augmented I-MAG; neither preserves a common basal selected DAG and all unknown-target regimes simultaneously.
statements.consumer: Residual circles in the sciPlex2 A549 analysis become certified nonidentifiabilities rather than artifacts of an incomplete orientation list.

statements.statement:
For every compatible encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), the enumerative algorithm satisfies \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\), is population sound and complete, and returns actual paired compatible certificates for every residual circle.  It terminates after checking at most \(3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}\) normalized certificates, with crude runtime
\[
O\!\left(3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}
\left[D^2 2^D+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
The observational output is on \(V\), each nonobservational certificate component is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), and no polynomial claim is made for this global search or for the conditional-independence and invariance queries needed to obtain \(\mathbf M\).  No completeness assertion is made for a fixed polynomial local CDIS calculus.
statements.justification: The result turns exact certificate realizability into a complete population procedure with explicit finite, nonpolynomial complexity.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention proves soundness of its local CDIS rules but not complete recovery of the full endpoint-invariance representative.
statements.consumer: Population benchmarking on sciPlex2 A549 perturbation regimes gains an exact target graph and auditable witness certificates from supplied oracle regime MAGs.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The encoded input in \(\texttt{def:oracle-input-encoding}\) is exactly the family consumed by \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\).  Applying \(\texttt{thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness}\) therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M),
\]
the certificate-count bound, and the corrected runtime
\[
O\!\left(
3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}
\left[D^2 2^D+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]
\right).
\]
The endpointwise feasible-mark identity in that theorem proves population soundness: every fixed output mark occurs in every compatible member.  It also proves population completeness: every invariant mark is fixed by the output, while every residual circle is accompanied by accepted tail and arrowhead certificates.  By \(\texttt{thm:finite-common-realizability}\), those certificates reconstruct actual members of the full common compatibility class.

The domain assertion follows directly from the two branches of \(\texttt{def:dai-certificate-checker}\): \(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R)\) is constructed on \(V\) and has no intervention indicator, whereas \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) is constructed on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) only for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\).  The procedure begins with supplied oracle matrices, so neither its correctness proof nor its runtime includes the conditional-independence and invariance queries used to discover those matrices.  Finally, the proof uses a generally doubly exponential global certificate search and never invokes a complete fixed local calculus.  Thus it entails neither a polynomial global-search claim nor completeness of a polynomial local CDIS calculus. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For Dai et al.'s two-variable regime family with \(K=1\) and intervention on the first variable, the selected collider model \(1\to S\leftarrow2\) and the unselected directed model \(2\to1\) belong to the same \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\). Consequently, the canonical observational edge has a circle at the endpoint of vertex \(1\) and a tail at the endpoint of vertex \(2\); no sound SI-PAG calculus may orient the first endpoint.
statements.justification: The smallest published equivalence witness fixes a nontrivial boundary that the completeness theorem must preserve.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention gives the compatible pair but does not state its endpoint-invariance consequence in a canonical SI-PAG.
statements.consumer: The proposition prevents a complete implementation from falsely resolving selection-induced association as causation in the simplest diagnostic case.
statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Proof.}
\emph{Construction of the boundary instance.}
Set \(D=2\), \(V=\{1,2\}\), and \(K=1\).  Consider
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{sel}}
 =\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{sel}},\{S\},(\varnothing,\{1\})\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{sel}}:\ 1\longrightarrow S\longleftarrow2,
\]
where \(S\) is binary and the observed stratum is \(S=1\), and
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{dir}}
 =\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{dir}},\varnothing,(\varnothing,\{1\})\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{dir}}:\ 2\longrightarrow1.
\]
These are the two candidates in the clinical two-variable witness of
\cite{DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention}.  Define the supplied oracle representatives by
\[
 \mathcal M^{(0)}:\ X_1\mathbin{---}X_2,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M^{(1)}:\
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2,
 \qquad
 \mathbf M=(\mathcal M^{(0)},\mathcal M^{(1)}).
 \tag{1}
\]
In accordance with the boundary convention in \(\texttt{def:twin-graph}\), the
observational representative has no intervention-indicator vertex.

Both basal graphs are finite DAGs and neither has a latent common cause of the two
system vertices.  In \(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\), the unique selection node is binary,
childless, and has only observed parents; for \(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), the corresponding
selection conditions are vacuous.  The observational target is empty and the sole
nonobservational target is \(\{1\}\) in both candidates.  Selection is imposed on the
basal copy, and the intervention changes only the mechanism of \(X_1\), while all
other mechanisms and exogenous inputs are shared.  Thus the structural member
conditions in \(\texttt{def:dai-compatible-class}\) hold.  It remains to calculate the
two regime projections.

For \(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\), the indicator-free observational graph is
\[
 X_1\longrightarrow S^*\longleftarrow X_2.
\]
After conditioning on \(S^*\), the displayed path induces an adjacency between the
two retained vertices.  Each endpoint is an ancestor of \(S^*\); hence the endpoint
rule in \(\texttt{def:mag-projection}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}}^{(0)}:
 X_1\mathbin{---}X_2.
 \tag{2}
\]
For target \(\{1\}\), the nonobservational twin graph has the relevant edges
\[
 \zeta_1\to X_1,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_1\to X_1,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_1\to X_1^*,
 \qquad
 X_1^*\to S^*,
 \qquad
 X_2\to S^*.
 \tag{3}
\]
Marginalizing \(X_1^*,\varepsilon_1\) and conditioning on \(S^*\), the path
\[
 X_1\leftarrow\varepsilon_1\to X_1^*\to S^*\leftarrow X_2
\]
induces \(X_2\to X_1\): its endpoint at \(X_2\) is a tail because \(X_2\) is an
ancestor of \(S^*\), and its endpoint at \(X_1\) is an arrowhead because \(X_1\) is
an ancestor of neither \(X_2\) nor \(S^*\).  The direct edge
\(\zeta_1\to X_1\) is retained.  There is no inducing path between \(\zeta_1\) and
\(X_2\): the only graph path between them contains the retained nonendpoint
\(X_1\) as the collider \(\zeta_1\to X_1\leftarrow\varepsilon_1\), and \(X_1\)
has no descendant in \(\{X_2\}\cup\{S^*\}\).  Consequently,
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}}^{(1)}:
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2.
 \tag{4}
\]

For \(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), there is neither marginalization nor conditioning in the
observational branch, so
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}}^{(0)}:
 X_2\longrightarrow X_1.
 \tag{5}
\]
In the target-\(1\) twin graph, the reality-world edges
\(\zeta_1\to X_1\) and \(X_2\to X_1\) are retained.  Every graph path from
\(\zeta_1\) to \(X_2\) contains the retained collider \(X_1\) as a nonendpoint,
and there is no selected vertex to activate that collider.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}}^{(1)}:
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2.
 \tag{6}
\]
The two observational MAGs in (2) and (5) are Markov equivalent: each has the
single adjacency \(X_1-X_2\), and a two-vertex graph has no unshielded triple or
discriminating path.  The two nonobservational MAGs in (4) and (6) are identical.
Thus both equivalence-match conditions hold, and therefore
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{sel}},\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}
 \in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M).
 \tag{7}
\]

\emph{Invariance of the endpoint at vertex \(2\).}
The pair in (7) alone shows noninvariance at vertex \(1\); to establish the claimed
tail at vertex \(2\), fix an arbitrary
\(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Observational equivalence to
\(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) gives the adjacency \(X_1-X_2\).  Interventional equivalence to
\(\mathcal M^{(1)}\) gives exactly the skeleton
\[
 \zeta_1-X_1-X_2,
 \qquad
 \zeta_1\not\sim X_2,
 \tag{8}
\]
and makes the unshielded triple in (8) a collider at \(X_1\).

Suppose for contradiction that the observational mark at the endpoint of \(X_2\)
were an arrowhead.  The observational projection retains both system vertices,
marginalizes no system or exogenous vertex, and conditions only on childless selection
sinks.  Since \(D=2\), a nondirect path between \(X_1\) and \(X_2\) can have only
selection vertices as nonendpoints.  Any such adjacency-producing path passes through
a selected common child, making both endpoints ancestors of the conditioned set and
therefore giving tails at both endpoints.  A bidirected edge cannot arise because causal
sufficiency excludes a latent common cause of \(X_1\) and \(X_2\).  The assumed
arrowhead at \(X_2\) must therefore come from the basal causal edge
\[
 1\longrightarrow2.
 \tag{9}
\]

Next, (8) determines the intervention target.  If
\(2\in I_\eta^{(1)}\), then \(\texttt{def:twin-graph}\) inserts the direct retained
edge \(\zeta_1\to X_2\), contradicting \(\zeta_1\not\sim X_2\).  If
\(I_\eta^{(1)}=\varnothing\), the exogenous indicator \(\zeta_1\) has no incident
edge at all, contradicting \(\zeta_1\sim X_1\).  As \(V=\{1,2\}\), these two
facts imply
\[
 I_\eta^{(1)}=\{1\}.
 \tag{10}
\]
By (9)--(10), the nonobservational twin graph contains the retained reality-world
edge \(X_1\to X_2\).  Thus \(X_1\) is an ancestor of \(X_2\), and the endpoint
rule of \(\texttt{def:mag-projection}\) puts a tail at \(X_1\) on their
interventional MAG edge.  This contradicts the arrowhead at \(X_1\) required by the
unshielded collider in (8).  Therefore the supposition was false, and
\[
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,2;12)}(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)})
 =\mathrm{tail}
 \quad\text{for every }\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M).
 \tag{11}
\]

\emph{Canonical marks and the soundness boundary.}
Equation (2) supplies a tail at the observational endpoint of \(X_1\), whereas
(5) supplies an arrowhead there.  By (7), both are compatible witnesses, so the
definition of the canonical SI-PAG gives a circle at that endpoint.  Equation (11)
and the same definition give a tail at the endpoint of \(X_2\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,1;12)}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\circ,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,2;12)}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\mathrm{tail}.
 \tag{12}
\]
A sound SI-PAG calculus may fix an endpoint only to a mark shared by every member
of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Fixing the first endpoint to a tail is refuted by
\(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), while fixing it to an arrowhead is refuted by
\(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\).  Thus no sound calculus may orient that endpoint.

This is a finite graphical boundary result.  No distributional support, positivity,
overlap, rank, division, inverse, or limiting condition is used.  The operative boundary
conditions are \(D=2\), \(K=1\), an indicator-free observational branch, and one
indicator-bearing intervention on vertex \(1\); nonemptiness of the compatibility class
is witnessed explicitly by (7).  \(\square\)

statements.statement:
If \(K=0\) and every compatible candidate has \(S_\eta=\varnothing\), then
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}^{(0)}(\mathbf M)
\]
is the ordinary CPDAG of the causally sufficient observational DAG Markov-equivalence class and therefore agrees endpointwise with complete PC/Meek orientation.  This is an extensional reduction of the output; it does not assert that the enumerative implementation runs in the polynomial time of PC.
statements.justification: The no-intervention, no-selection boundary verifies the exact output against the standard CPDAG without conflating algorithms or runtimes.
statements.gap: The reduction is classical, but it checks that the coupled certificate semantics adds no endpoint information in the ordinary DAG case.
statements.consumer: Existing CPDAG software supplies an endpointwise regression oracle for the zero-regime boundary.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\) be a normalized certificate, let \(A=\operatorname{an}_E(\bigcup H)\), and let \(F_k=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)\).  For the causally sufficient, childless-selection, pre-treatment twin construction, Dai et al.'s MAG formulas give exactly the observational adjacencies, interventional path-induced adjacencies, indicator adjacencies, and endpoint orientations used to construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R)\) in \(\texttt{def:dai-certificate-checker}\).  Moreover, two such basal-DAG and ordered-target families are Markov equivalent across all regimes if and only if their corresponding regime MAGs have the same adjacencies and unshielded collider triples in every regime.

attestation.note: Scope checked against the ICLR 2025 proceedings; the node is a faithful synthesis of the located formulas and equivalence criterion, not a verbatim quotation.

statements.justification: The checker must use the published twin-MAG formulas and special adjacency-and-v-structure equivalence reduction rather than treating them as consequences of a construction definition.
statements.gap: This is cited substrate from DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention, not a new result of the note.
statements.consumer: The normalization and common-realizability proofs use one auditable source node for every published graph-construction fact.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), deleting all but one childless selection node for each distinct parent set produces a candidate \(\bar\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) with exactly the same observational and nonobservational projected MAGs.  The candidate \(\bar\eta\) has a normalized certificate \(\mathcal R_{\bar\eta}=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+})\) with \(|H|\le 2^D\).
statements.justification: Removing duplicate selection-parent sets makes the common-realization search finite without changing any regime projection.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention allows multiple childless selection nodes but does not isolate this finite normalization.
statements.consumer: The enumerator needs the uniform bound \(|H|\le 2^D\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Put \(E=\mathcal G_\eta[V]\), let
\[
H=\{\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(s):s\in S_\eta\},
\qquad
T_k=I_\eta^{(k)}\quad(k\in\mathcal K_+),
\]
where the braces in the definition of \(H\) discard multiplicity.  By \(\operatorname{ass{:}selection\text{-}parents}\), every element of \(H\) is a subset of \(V\).  There are only \(2^D\) subsets of \(V\), so \(|H|\le 2^D\).

Construct \(\bar\eta\) by retaining \(E\), the ordered targets, and one binary childless selection node \(s_h\) with parent set \(h\) for each \(h\in H\).  This preserves finiteness, acyclicity, causal sufficiency among vertices in \(V\), binary selection, childlessness, observed selection parents, the selected-stratum convention, pre-treatment timing, the empty observational target, and soft-intervention modularity.  It remains to verify the graphical projections.

The set of observed ancestors of selection is unchanged, because in either candidate it is
\[
A=\operatorname{an}_E\!\left(\bigcup_{h\in H}h\right).
\]
For each regime, the affected set \(F_k=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)\) is also unchanged.  Multiplicity of a selection node with a given parent set affects neither the assertion that \(i,j\) share a selected child nor any of the sets \(A,F_k\).  The observational adjacency formula, every interventional path-induced adjacency, every indicator adjacency, and every endpoint-orientation case in \(\texttt{lem:dai-certificate-mag-characterization}\) therefore has the same truth value for \(\eta\) and \(\bar\eta\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal M_{\eta}^{(k)}=\mathcal M_{\bar\eta}^{(k)}
\qquad\text{for every }k\in\mathcal K.
\]
Since \(\eta\) matches the supplied representatives, so does \(\bar\eta\), proving \(\bar\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  The tuple \((E,H,(T_k))\) is the required normalized certificate. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Assume \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).  A normalized certificate \(\mathcal R\) passes \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)\) if and only if its canonical reconstruction is a member of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Every member of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) has an equivalent passing normalized certificate, and every passing certificate reconstructs a compatible member.  Consequently,
\[
\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists\mathcal R\;\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1.
\]
statements.justification: This establishes that a finite accepted object is exactly a common basal-DAG realization, rather than an unrelated collection of regime-wise MAG completions.
statements.gap: The published equivalence criterion is pairwise graphical; it does not package a finite exact checker over unknown selection structures and targets.
statements.consumer: Every feasible endpoint mark and every witness returned by the population algorithm is backed by a reconstructible member of the full compatibility class.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix a normalized certificate
\[
\mathcal R=(E,H,(T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}).
\]
Its canonical reconstruction \(\eta_{\mathcal R}\) is obtained as follows.  On the observed vertices use the directed acyclic graph \(E\).  For each \(h\in H\), add a distinct binary vertex \(s_h\), add precisely the arrows \(i\to s_h\) with \(i\in h\), and give \(s_h\) no children.  Set
\[
I_{\eta_{\mathcal R}}^{(0)}=\varnothing,
\qquad
I_{\eta_{\mathcal R}}^{(k)}=T_k
\quad(k\in\mathcal K_+).
\]
Choose mutually independent exogenous inputs for the observed-variable mechanisms.  For each selection node take an independent \(U_h\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and use the binary structural kernel
\[
s_h=\mathbf 1\{U_h\le 1/2\}.
\]
The structural equation may take \((X_i)_{i\in h}\) as formal parent arguments; no causal-minimality condition is imposed by \(\texttt{def:dai-compatible-class}\), so this choice preserves the declared graphical parent set \(h\).  Conditional on the observed variables,
\[
\Pr\!\left((s_h)_{h\in H}=\mathbf 1\mid X_V\right)=2^{-|H|}>0,
\]
including the boundary case \(H=\varnothing\), where the probability is one.  Thus conditioning on the selected stratum is well-defined.  Finally, in regime \(k\), retain the basal mechanism and exogenous input outside \(T_k\), and choose an arbitrary soft replacement on every vertex in \(T_k\).

Because \(E\) is acyclic and \(H\) is finite with \(|H|\le 2^D\), this construction is a finite DAG.  The independent observed-variable exogenous inputs give causal sufficiency on \(V\); the new selection nodes are binary, childless, and have only observed parents; the positive selected stratum, basal timing, empty observational target, and modular soft replacements verify the remaining structural clauses of \(\texttt{def:dai-compatible-class}\).  By \(\texttt{lem:dai-certificate-mag-characterization}\), the projected regime family of \(\eta_{\mathcal R}\) is exactly
\[
\mathbf N(\mathcal R)
=\bigl(\mathcal N^{(0)}(\mathcal R),\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)}(\mathcal R)\bigr).
\]

We first prove the checker equivalence.  If \(\eta_{\mathcal R}\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), then every \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) is Markov equivalent to \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\).  Markov-equivalent MAGs have the same adjacencies and the same unshielded collider triples.  Therefore every component comparison in \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}\) succeeds, and
\[
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1.
\]

Conversely, suppose that \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\).  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:compatible-input}\) supplies an anchor \(\eta_0\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), compatibility of \(\eta_0\) implies that \(\mathcal M_{\eta_0}^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacencies and unshielded collider triples.  Checker acceptance gives the same conclusion for \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal M_{\eta_0}^{(k)}
\]
have identical adjacency and unshielded-collider patterns in every regime.  Both families arise from the causally sufficient, childless-selection, pre-treatment twin construction.  The cross-regime equivalence clause of \(\texttt{lem:dai-certificate-mag-characterization}\) therefore yields
\[
\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)
\equiv_m \mathcal M_{\eta_0}^{(k)}
\equiv_m \mathcal M^{(k)}
\qquad(k\in\mathcal K).
\]
All non-equivalence clauses of the class were already verified in the explicit reconstruction.  Thus \(\eta_{\mathcal R}\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).

It remains to relate arbitrary compatible candidates to normalized certificates.  If \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), then \(\texttt{lem:selection-normalization}\) produces \(\bar\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) with the same projected MAGs and a normalized certificate \(\mathcal R_{\bar\eta}\).  The forward implication just proved gives
\[
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\bar\eta},\mathbf M)=1.
\]
Conversely, every passing certificate has just been shown to reconstruct a member of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Consequently, nonemptiness of the class produces a passing certificate, while a passing certificate produces a member of the class.  Hence
\[
\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists\mathcal R\;\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1.
\]
No division, rank, overlap, or boundary condition is used; the only positivity needed for the constructed conditioning event was verified directly above. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every compatible oracle family \(\mathbf M\), normalized-certificate enumeration in \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\) terminates and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M).
\]
For every endpoint left circular, the retained tail and arrowhead certificates reconstruct two members of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) that agree with every fixed output mark and realize the two opposite marks at that endpoint.  The enumeration visits at most
\[
3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}
\]
certificates and admits the crude finite runtime bound
\[
O\!\left(3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}
\left[D^2 2^D+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
This is an exact, generally doubly exponential population algorithm, not a polynomial local-rule completeness result.
statements.justification: Endpointwise feasible-mark enumeration gives a computable semantic representative and actual global witnesses for every noninvariant mark.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention leaves a complete local calculus open; this theorem supplies exact completeness by finite common-realization search instead.
statements.consumer: The sciPlex2 A549 workflow can interpret a residual circle as certified nonidentifiability over the full pre-treatment-selection class, subject to oracle regime MAG input.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For every unordered pair of vertices in \(V\), a directed graph \(E\) has one of three states: no edge, the first direction, or the second direction.  Thus there are at most
\[
3^{\binom D2}
\]
candidate directed graphs, and filtering them for acyclicity retains every possible DAG.  There are \(2^{2^D}\) choices of \(H\subseteq 2^V\), and there are \(2^{DK}\) ordered choices of \((T_k)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\).  Therefore the lexicographic enumeration is finite and visits at most
\[
3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}
\]
normalized certificates.

Define the finite accepted set
\[
\mathfrak A(\mathbf M)
=\{\mathcal R:\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R,\mathbf M)=1\}.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:compatible-input}\) and \(\texttt{thm:finite-common-realizability}\), this set is nonempty.  Fix an endpoint \(e=(k,u;uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\).  The same theorem, together with \(\texttt{lem:selection-normalization}\) as used in its proof, gives the exact feasible-mark identity
\[
\left\{
\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R)\bigr):
\mathcal R\in\mathfrak A(\mathbf M)
\right\}
=
\left\{
\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\bigr):
\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)
\right\}.
\]
Indeed, an accepted certificate reconstructs a compatible candidate, which proves inclusion from left to right.  Conversely, every compatible candidate has a passing normalized certificate with exactly the same projected MAGs, which proves inclusion from right to left.

Every fully oriented MAG endpoint is a tail or an arrowhead.  The common set in the last display is therefore exactly one of
\[
\{\mathrm{tail}\},
\qquad
\{\mathrm{arrow}\},
\qquad
\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]
The output rule in \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\) assigns, respectively, a tail, an arrowhead, or a circle.  These are exactly the endpointwise cases in \(\texttt{def:canonical-si-pag}\).  The checker also enforces the supplied skeleton in every regime.  Hence, endpoint by endpoint,
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M).
\]

If the output endpoint \(e\) is circular, its feasible-mark set contains both marks.  Finiteness of the enumeration therefore supplies a first accepted tail certificate and a first accepted arrowhead certificate.  By \(\texttt{thm:finite-common-realizability}\), their canonical reconstructions are members of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  At every fixed output endpoint, the feasible-mark set is a singleton, so both reconstructions agree with that fixed mark.  At \(e\), the two reconstructions realize opposite marks.  They are thus the required paired common-basal-DAG witnesses, not unrelated regime-wise MAG completions.

We finally account for runtime.  For one certificate, materializing every selected parent set and all unordered co-parent pairs costs
\[
O\!\left(\sum_{h\in H}|h|^2\right)
\le O(D^2 2^D).
\]
Computing the transitive closure of \(E\), the sets \(A(\mathcal R)\) and \(F_k(\mathcal R)\), the observational adjacency and mark matrices, and the regime-specific connectivity conditions in \(\texttt{def:dai-certificate-checker}\) costs
\[
O\bigl((K+1)(D+1)^3\bigr).
\]
The same cubic envelope covers enumeration and comparison of unshielded triples.  Updating all feasible-mark sets and retaining the first opposing witnesses costs \(O(N_{\mathrm{end}})\) per certificate.  Multiplying the sum of these per-certificate bounds by the certificate-count bound gives
\[
O\!\left(
3^{\binom D2}2^{2^D+DK}
\left[D^2 2^D+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]
\right).
\]
This is a finite, generally doubly exponential population computation.  It is not a polynomial local-rule algorithm and says nothing about the cost of obtaining the oracle regime MAGs by conditional-independence or invariance queries. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For a finite causally sufficient DAG Markov-equivalence class, the completed partially directed acyclic graph has a directed edge exactly when that direction is common to every DAG in the class and an undirected edge otherwise; complete PC/Meek orientation returns this same endpoint-invariance representative.

source.locator: Completeness theorem and the causally sufficient DAG specialization

statements.justification: The zero-regime sanity check uses the classical endpoint-invariance characterization of a CPDAG.
statements.gap: This is standard graphical-model substrate, not a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It identifies the enumerative output with complete PC/Meek orientation in the no-selection observational boundary.

sampling_model.design: Population-oracle graphical input; there is no sampling randomness in the proposal kernel.
sampling_model.units: A finite observed vertex set \(V\) shared by one observational and \(K\) soft-intervention regimes.
sampling_model.treatment: The observational regime has no indicator and target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\); only \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) has indicator \(\zeta_k\) and unknown target \(I_\eta^{(k)}\), with intervention after basal selection.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable to the population graphical theorem.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The oracle regime MAG representatives are supplied. Their discovery by conditional-independence and invariance tests is outside the complexity claim.

estimand_functional: On compatible oracle families, \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\), where \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}\) is the normalized-certificate enumeration in \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 proves soundness of the marks returned by oracle CDIS, while Lemmas 3--6 and Theorem 2 give the regime-MAG construction and equivalence substrate.
Complete FCI orients every invariant endpoint in one ordinary MAG equivalence class.
The unknown-target soft-intervention completeness theory excludes selection bias.
The paper studies orientation completeness with background knowledge inside restricted MAG settings.
Theorem 4 gives F-FCI completeness under post-treatment selection and different F-PAG semantics.

tldr: Selective enrollment precedes intervention in many perturbation studies, so one indicator-free observational MAG on \(V\) and the nonobservational MAGs on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) are coupled projections of one unobserved basal-world DAG rather than independent equivalence classes. The project defines the canonical SI-PAG as endpoint-mark invariance over Dai et al.'s full causally sufficient compatibility class and isolates the open construction of a finite sound within- and cross-regime calculus with globally compatible opposing witnesses for every residual circle. Resolving that extension problem yields mark completeness and complete population CDIS, with a finite matrix input, a cost for matching each rule, and a polynomial total orientation-closure certificate, while making no polynomial claim for conditional-independence discovery.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize pre-treatment-selection interventional equivalence and prove oracle CDIS soundness, but explicitly leave both a graphical representative of the equivalence class and CDIS completeness open.
project_justification.niche: Ordinary FCI completeness treats one MAG class, and \(\Psi\)-FCI completeness treats unknown soft targets without the basal selection world; neither supplies paired realizations that preserve all of Dai's cross-regime twin constraints.
project_justification.fill: The project isolates a twin-compatible extension lemma, uses it to equate finitely encoded monotone rule closure with semantic endpoint invariance, and packages the result as complete population discovery with an explicit per-rule and total oracle-input orientation cost.

related_work: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention supplies the published twin-graph semantics coupling an indicator-free observational regime to indicator-bearing nonobservational regimes, the adjacency-and-v-structure equivalence theorem, the two-variable selection-versus-causation witness, and a sound but not complete CDIS procedure. Zhang2008CompleteFCI supplies the discriminating-path and circle-component proof architecture for a single observational MAG class. JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020 supplies an augmented intervention-MAG realizability lemma and paired endpoint witnesses for unknown soft targets, but its tail-completeness argument explicitly excludes selection bias. AliRichardsonSpirtes2009 supplies the ordered-collider equivalence criterion that explains why ordinary MAG reasoning must be checked before exploiting Dai's special reduction. VenkateswaranPerkovic2026 and WangDuZhou2025 show that generic background-knowledge closure requires additional dense-graph rules and remains distinct from globally coupled twin realizability. LuoEtAl2026PostTreatmentSelection gives a complete F-PAG for selection after intervention, whose square marks and inducing-node semantics do not represent Dai's basal selection. ColomboMaathuisKalischRichardson2012 is relevant only to a later finite-sample rung; the present kernel begins with finitely encoded oracle regime MAGs and bounds only their orientation closure.
technical_internal_limitation: Independent within-regime MAG completions are not accepted as compatibility witnesses: every completion used by the calculus must be realized by one basal DAG and one ordered unknown-target family. A generic non-two-variable finite obstruction family and its calculus certificate remain open diagnostics rather than theorem contributions in this core.
honest_scope: The theorem-level target is population mark completeness on Dai et al.'s published causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection class, with regime zero projected on \(V\) without an intervention indicator and each regime in \(\mathcal K_+\) projected on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The finite rule construction and globally compatible paired-witness lemma are open. The stated polynomial certificate covers matrix initialization and orientation-rule closure from supplied oracle MAGs; finite-sample consistency, latent common causes, post-treatment filtering, effect identification, and the number of conditional-independence or invariance queries used to discover those MAGs are outside the claim. In the no-intervention, no-selection special case, the construction must collapse to the ordinary CPDAG.
